rationale: One major finding: the two new creation pages use inconsistent post-save navigation. NewProjectSchedulerPage uses router.push({ name: 'schedulers' }) (deterministic) while NewUserSchedulerPage uses navigateBack(SCHEDULERS) (history-based, may not land on the schedulers list if the user arrived via direct URL). Both pages also call schedulersStore.fetchSchedulers() with no query args inside setTimeout(..., 1000) — redundant since SchedulersPage re-fetches on mount. All other acceptance criteria (route registration, SettingsForm reuse, hideType field hiding, titles, store methods, Create button) are satisfied. Deferred: CronInputField preview is blur-only (UX, not a correctness bug). Dismissed: 7 blind/edge-case findings that were either based on incorrect project assumptions (useVueRouter is an internal hook) or pre-existing issues outside this PR's scope.

findings.problem: NewProjectSchedulerPage uses router.push({ name: 'schedulers' }) for post-save navigation while NewUserSchedulerPage uses navigateBack(SCHEDULERS). The two new pages navigate to the same destination via different mechanisms: navigateBack calls router.back() and only falls through to SCHEDULERS when no history entry exists. When a user creates a user scheduler after a fresh page load or via a direct URL, there may be no history entry and behavior becomes browser-dependent. Additionally, both pages call schedulersStore.fetchSchedulers() with no query args inside setTimeout(..., 1000), fetching with empty params that ignore any active filters or ownerType — and the call is redundant since SchedulersPage already re-fetches on mount.
findings.impact: Users arriving at /schedulers/user/new via direct URL get inconsistent post-save navigation. The redundant setTimeout fetchSchedulers() call also causes a brief flash of unfiltered results before SchedulersPage issues its own filtered query.
findings.recommendation: Standardize both pages to use the same navigation strategy. The simplest fix: replace navigateBack(SCHEDULERS) in NewUserSchedulerPage with router.push({ name: 'schedulers' }) to match the project page. Remove the setTimeout(() => schedulersStore.fetchSchedulers(), 1000) calls from both pages — SchedulersPage re-fetches on mount via useEffect([query]) and the delay is unnecessary.
